## Purpose and entry points
OpenBao is a Go-based secrets-management server: encrypted storage, dynamic credentials, cryptographic operations, leasing/revocation, auditing, and policy-controlled access. The `bao` executable starts at `main.go`, dispatches CLI/server behavior through `internal/command/main.go` and `internal/command/commands.go`. Public Go integration surfaces are the versioned API client and plugin SDK under `api/client.go` and `sdk/logical/logical.go`.

## Server bootstrap and transport
`bao server` parses server configuration, constructs listeners, storage, sealing, telemetry, and the Vault core. Server-specific configuration and TCP/Unix listener setup live in `internal/command/server/config.go`, `internal/command/server/listener_tcp.go`, and `internal/command/server/listener_unix.go`. HTTP requests enter the API handler in `internal/http/handler.go`; logical and system endpoint translation is separated into `internal/http/logical.go` and `internal/http/sys_health.go`.

## Core request control plane
`internal/vault/core.go` is the central runtime coordinator. Requests flow: HTTP/CLI/API client → authenticated core request handling → policy/capability checks → mount router → selected backend → encrypted storage and response/audit processing. Routing by mounted path is defined by `internal/vault/routing/router.go` and `internal/vault/routing/mount_table.go`. Authentication, token lifecycle, ACL policy evaluation, identity, quotas, and response wrapping are core boundaries in `internal/vault/auth.go`, `internal/vault/token_store.go`, and `internal/vault/policy/acl.go`.

## Security lifecycle, storage, and HA
Persistent logical data is protected by the barrier encryption layer before reaching physical storage; keyring and AES-GCM behavior are in `internal/vault/barrier/barrier.go`, `internal/vault/barrier/keyring.go`, and `internal/vault/barrier/aes_gcm.go`. Seal/unseal and auto-seal management are in `internal/vault/seal.go`, `internal/vault/seal_manager.go`, and `internal/vault/seal_autoseal.go`. Supported in-repo physical implementations include in-memory, PebbleDB, PostgreSQL, and integrated Raft: `internal/physical/inmem/inmem.go`, `internal/physical/pebbledb/pebbledb.go`, `internal/physical/postgresql/postgresql.go`, `internal/physical/raft/raft.go`. Raft supplies replicated storage, snapshots, and cluster membership; forwarding handles requests requiring an active node via `internal/vault/forwarding/request_forwarding.go`.

## Mounted auth, secret, and audit backends
Backends implement the extensible logical interface and are mounted dynamically. The SDK contracts are in `sdk/logical/logical.go` and `sdk/framework/backend.go`. Built-ins include auth methods (AppRole, JWT/OIDC, Kubernetes, user/password) under `internal/builtin/credential/approle/backend.go`, `internal/builtin/credential/jwt/backend.go`, and `internal/builtin/credential/kubernetes/backend.go`; secret engines including KV, PKI/ACME, transit cryptography, database credentials, SSH, and Kubernetes under `internal/builtin/logical/kv/backend.go`, `internal/builtin/logical/pki/backend.go`, and `internal/builtin/logical/transit/backend.go`. Lease registration, renewal, expiry, and revocation are centralized in `internal/vault/expiration.go`. Audit events are brokered by `internal/vault/audit_broker.go` and sent to configurable file, HTTP, socket, or syslog devices.

## Plugin and external-service boundaries
Plugins can run out of process over gRPC; catalog and reload control are in `internal/vault/plugin_catalog.go` and `internal/vault/plugin_reload.go`, while protocol/server adapters are in `sdk/plugin/grpc_backend.go`. Database plugins integrate with Cassandra, InfluxDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Valkey; the logical database engine orchestrates credential generation and rollback in `internal/builtin/logical/database/backend.go`. Other external boundaries include Kubernetes API authentication/service registration, OIDC/JWT providers, KMS/HSM seal providers, network audit sinks, and PostgreSQL storage.

## Auxiliary clients and UI
The CLI uses the API client for operational, auth, secrets, policy, and Raft commands, with command implementations under `internal/command/`. Agent/proxy mode can auto-authenticate, template secrets, write token sinks, and cache/proxy API traffic via `internal/command/agent.go` and `internal/command/agentproxyshared/cache/proxy.go`. A separate Ember web UI in `ui/` communicates with the same HTTP API; routing begins at `ui/app/router.js`, and API adaptation at `ui/app/adapters/application.js`. The repository also contains a separate Docusaurus documentation site under `website/docusaurus.config.ts`.
